subject: Request: short version-lock exemption for spectre-3b-cpu-light variant
messages:
From: Sonia Lopez <sonia.lopez@finco.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: New variant onboard + short version-lock ask

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. FinCo is ready to move forward with the spectre-3b-cpu-light variant for our internal knowledge-base indexing workload. The vendor team has asked that we keep the serving binary tied to the spectre-3b-v2 family for the first 14 days after rollout while they validate telemetry on their side. They call this a "short version-lock" for the variant.

Can Redwood accommodate a 14-day version-lock exemption (i.e., prevent auto-roll forward to newer compatible variants) for the spectre-3b-cpu-light variant during the canary window? Our asks:
- Compatibility check with our typical 4k-token mixed request profile
- Baseline telemetry capture (latency, error-rate, token-cost) for the first 72h canary
- A rollback plan if latency/regressions exceed thresholds (we suggest 20% p99 latency increase or >2% generation-errors)

I attached the vendor compatibility matrix and a short telemetry snapshot from our staging runs. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Sonia
Sonia Lopez
Head of AI Ops, FinCo
sonia.lopez@finco.com

Attachments: spectre-3b-compat-matrix.csv, telemetry-snapshot-20270614.txt

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sonia Lopez <sonia.lopez@finco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New variant onboard + short version-lock ask

Hi Sonia — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. Looping in Marissa, Laura, and Dev to confirm feasibility and the exact gating we'll put in place.

Quick summary of our immediate plan:
1) Laura and Dev will run a compatibility pre-check against our staging dataset and surface any missing kernel/path issues.
2) If green, we can schedule a 72h canary in our us-west cluster with telemetry capture.
3) We can enable a temporary "version-lock exemption" for up to 14 days under a canary guardrail (automatic rollback policy + telemetry alerts).

Two clarifying questions for FinCo:
- Can you confirm the traffic profile for the canary (QPS, average prompt size, and % of streaming vs non-streaming)?
- Are you expecting Redwood to hold the binary pin on the public catalog, or just for your Dedicated/Private pool?

Cc: Marissa — if we proceed, please confirm the org-level approval required for a temporary catalog-level lock vs. a customer-scoped lock.

Thanks,
Monica
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: New variant onboard + short version-lock ask

On Mon, 14 Jun 2027 at 09:12 AM Sonia Lopez <sonia.lopez@finco.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. FinCo is ready to move forward with the spectre-3b-cpu-light variant...

I ran the compatibility pre-checks against FinCo's staging samples and the attached compat matrix. Summary of findings:
- Runtime: spectre-3b-cpu-light lacks optimized AVX512 kernels in our current release; it degrades p95/p99 under sustained streaming loads.
- Tokenizer: no changes required.
- KV cache: standard behavior, but memory pressure increases by ~12% in our sim (see telemetry-snapshot).
- Safety hooks: no incompatibilities.

Risk assessment and mitigation:
- Risk: 10-15% p99 latency uplift during the first 24-48h under mixed streaming.
- Mitigation: enable workload-aware batching cap, reduce default max-seq for the canary, and restrict canary QPS to 5qps initially.
- Telemetry: we'll capture p50/p95/p99, error-rate, token-cost, and model-variant fallbacks every 15m; set automated alert if p99 > baseline * 1.20 or error-rate > 2%.

Ask: I can implement a customer-scoped temporary version-lock for FinCo's Dedicated pool for up to 14 days with an automated rollback trigger and an alerting runbook. However, catalog-level locks require Marissa/Product sign-off because they affect the public model catalog.

Attachments: detailed compat diff (spectre-3b-compat-matrix.csv), staging telemetry (telemetry-snapshot-20270614.txt).

If approved, I'll schedule the 72h canary to start Wed 06/16 08:00 PT and will shepherd the rollout.

— Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sonia Lopez <sonia.lopez@finco.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: New variant onboard + short version-lock ask

Thanks everyone for the quick work here.

Decision: approve a customer-scoped temporary version-lock exemption for FinCo's Dedicated pool for 14 days, conditional on the following:
- Dev to implement automated rollback at the first alert breach (p99 > 1.20x baseline OR error-rate > 2%).
- Canary to be limited to 5 QPS for first 24h, then ramp to 20 QPS if no alerts.
- Laura to own the canary playbook and confirm the telemetry dashboard before start.
- Legal/sales: Monica, please confirm with FinCo whether they expect the lock to be reflected in our public catalog or only at the customer allocation level; we will not change public catalog entries without product leadership approval.

Marissa
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
